material_definitions: A systematic study of Li(1+x)M(x)Ti(2-x)(PO4)3 with M=Al, Cr and Fe and 0 <= x <= 1 has been carried out.
The analysis showed that lithium atoms occupy the well-known M1 position and a new position called M2'.
The addition of trivalent metals into the LiTi2(PO4)3 compound gives rise to the liberation of the M1 sites and simultaneous occupation of the M2' sites.
The highest conductivity was found in the sample Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3.
The material series investigated are Li-ion conductors based on the NASICON structure, generally Li(1+x)M(x)Ti(2-x)(PO4)3 where M is Al, Cr, or Fe.
Conductivity measurements were performed using complex impedance spectroscopy to separate bulk dc and grain boundary contributions.
The maximum conductivity was found in the sample Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3.
The bulk conductivity values are typically two or three orders of magnitude larger than those of the grain boundary.
